self_assessment: Implemented U2FAuthenticateChallenge (embedding *u2f.AuthenticateChallenge for flat backward-compatible JSON plus a Challenges []u2f.AuthenticateChallenge list) exactly as specified in lib/auth/auth.go, rewrote U2FSignRequest to build one challenge per registered U2F device instead of returning on the first match, propagated the new return type through ServerWithRoles/Client/ClientI/lib-web sessionCache, updated the tsh-side CLI login flow (lib/client/weblogin.go SSHAgentU2FLogin) to try all challenges via the already-variadic u2f.AuthenticateSignChallenge with a fallback to the legacy single field, and hid the pre-existing `tsh mfa` command tree via kingpin's existing .Hidden() mechanism (used elsewhere in tool/tsh/tsh.go) since multi-device MFA management isn't fully done; go build and go vet are clean on lib/auth/..., lib/client/..., lib/web/..., tool/tsh/..., and I verified marshal/unmarshal compatibility with a standalone script, but could not run the repo's own U2F-related go tests (lib/web TestU2FLogin/TestChangePasswordWithTokenU2F) because they panic in NewTestAuthServer on this Go 1.24 toolchain due to a pre-existing vendored json-iterator/reflect2 incompatibility that reproduces identically on the unmodified base commit, so that test path is unverified beyond static compilation and manual review; I did not find or touch any TypeScript/web-UI frontend for this challenge type since none exists in this Go-only checkout at the base commit.
